items.setting: Campus copy center, self-service counter; a staff member speaks with a student making copies.

worlds.keyAct: adapts the plan to the shortage
worlds.line: The color copier is out of toner until the delivery comes Thursday.
worlds.reply: I'll print these flyers in black and white today then.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The staffer reports the color copier is down, so switching the flyers to black and white is the natural adjustment. Naming a campus card answers a payment question that was never asked, and stacking originals complies with a request nobody made. Choosing double-sided because prices match responds to a pricing note that was never given.

kills.1: Announcing the machine is "out of toner" asks nothing about payment, so naming a campus card answers a question never posed.
kills.2: "The color copier" being empty is a supply report, not a request to clear space, so promising to stack originals complies with nothing said.
kills.3: News that toner is gone "until the delivery" comes says nothing about pricing, so choosing double-sided because costs are equal has no basis here.

worlds.keyAct: answers the either-or with a choice

worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The staffer asks cash or card, and picking the campus card answers that either-or directly. Printing in black and white responds to a toner problem nobody reported, and stacking originals complies with a request never made. A remark about double-sided costing the same reacts to pricing information that was never stated.
